## Overview

ASUS Republic of Gamers and its hardware partner XREAL have begun worldwide shipping of the ROG XREAL R1, a pair of tethered gaming AR glasses that the companies describe as "the world's first 240Hz micro-OLED gaming AR glasses," [according to ASUS](https://press.asus.com/news/press-releases/rog-xreal-r1-gaming-ar-glasses-240hz-micro-oled/). editor_notes.content_quality: Clean, well-structured consumer-hardware brief: Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis. Word count 567 fits the News range (400-1200). The spec dump is dense but every figure is attributed inline, and the article correctly frames ASUS's marketing superlative ('the companies describe as "the world's first 240Hz micro-OLED gaming AR glasses"') rather than asserting it in the paper's own voice. The 'What We Don't Know' section responsibly flags that 240Hz is quoted 'with boosted frame rate enabled' and 700 nits 'with increased brightness enabled', and that the device is 3DoF rather than 6DoF-class VR.
editor_notes.source_verification: 5 sources cited; chief:review captured 4 snapshots (source-0..3); source-4 (Eneba) failed with 'Timeout after 15000ms' and has file:null in the manifest. I read every captured snapshot from disk (gunzip'd HTML, text-extracted). source-0.html.gz (ASUS 'Global Availability' / 240Hz micro-OLED release): CONFIRMS world's first 240Hz 0.01ms micro-OLED, Sony 0.55" micro-OLED, 1920x1080, FOV 57°, motion-to-photon 3ms, 700 nits (with increased brightness enabled), 106% sRGB, 240Hz (with boosted frame rate enabled), native 3DoF, electrochromic lens, Sound by Bose, 2D-to-3D conversion, Anchor/Follow, 171" virtual display, AND independently states 'Pre-orders open May 15, 2026' and 'worldwide shipping starting June 1, 2026'. source-1.html.gz (CES / Jan-5-2026 Las Vegas announcement release): CONFIRMS 91 grams weight, '3 ms motion-to-photon latency', 'LAS VEGAS, January 5, 2026', world's first 240Hz, and dock spec 2x HDMI 2.0 + 1x DisplayPort 1.4 + USB-C output. source-2.html.gz (ROG product page): CONFIRMS 240Hz/0.01ms response time, 171-inch virtual screen at 4 meters, 57° FOV, 700 nits, 106% sRGB, HDMI 2.0 x2 + DisplayPort 1.4, USB-C plug-and-play with ROG Ally integration ('allowing Ally to directly control the glasses'), Anchor & Follow Mode, three manually adjustable electrochromic tint levels (3-level dimming), ROG Control Dock. source-3.html.gz (Gizmodo): CONFIRMS $849 price and the exact quotes used — '$200 more than the $650 MSRP for the Xreal One Pro' (verbatim), dock 'two via HDMI 2.0 and one through DisplayPort 1.4' (verbatim), and 'spec for spec[...]the same, except for that refresh rate and the slightly more gamer-y design' (verbatim, with a correctly-marked ellipsis eliding 'the Xreal R1 and the Xreal One Pro are'). source-4 (Eneba) snapshot FAILED (timeout); it is cited only for the June-1-2026 shipping date and May-15-2026 pre-order date, and BOTH are independently confirmed verbatim in the captured source-0 (ASUS) release — so no claim rests solely on the unverifiable source. I did not re-WebFetch.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every headline/summary/lead specific traces to a captured source: 'first 240Hz micro-OLED gaming AR glasses' is ASUS's own claim (source-0/source-1), dual 1080p / 240Hz / micro-OLED / $849 / June-1 shipping all confirmed. No hallucinated numbers or quotes found. One minor framing point, not an error: ASUS's source-0 spec table lists 'Native 3DoF / 6DoF supported', while the article characterizes the device as '3DoF rather than full positional (6DoF) tracking'; the article's positive claim ('native 3DoF') is exactly correct and the 6DoF caveat is a reasonable editorial read, so no correction is warranted. Similarly, 'first appeared at CES 2026' is a fair characterization of the Jan-5-2026 Las Vegas pre-show announcement the sources document (CES 2026 ran Jan 6-9 in Las Vegas); date and location are sourced.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional. Marketing superlatives are attributed to ASUS, not adopted; the Analysis section situates the product as a display accessory (no onboard compute/AI) versus standalone Android XR glasses without cheerleading. No AI self-reference.
editor_notes.originality: Not a duplicate. The only related prior article (2026-05/19 Google I/O Android XR glasses) covers Google's Gemini-powered Android XR platform where XREAL appears merely as a partner and its unrelated Project Aura headset; the ROG XREAL R1 is a distinct product with a distinct event (worldwide shipping). Genuinely new coverage.
concerns: Three cited domains are off the source allowlist (press.asus.com, rog.asus.com, eneba.com). ASUS's own press/product pages are the legitimate first-party source for a product's own specs, so this is acceptable for spec reporting; I did not modify the allowlist. Eneba is a game-key marketplace blog (weaker outlet) but is cited only for two dates that ASUS itself confirms.

The Eneba snapshot (source-4) failed to capture (15s timeout), leaving it unverifiable from disk. Mitigated: its only two attributed facts (June 1 shipping, May 15 pre-orders) are both independently confirmed verbatim in the captured ASUS source-0 snapshot, so no claim is left unsupported.
recommendations: For a stronger provenance chain, the June-1 shipping and May-15 pre-order dates could have been cited directly to the ASUS release (source-0), which states both explicitly, rather than to the weaker Eneba blog whose snapshot failed.
Editorially consider whether ASUS press/product domains merit allowlisting for first-party product-spec reporting; not actioned here (allowlist left unmodified by policy).
editor_notes.overall_assessment: APPROVE. This is an accurate, well-sourced, neutrally-written consumer-hardware brief. Every spec, price, date, and the 'world's first 240Hz' superlative is corroborated by a captured, credible snapshot, and the two automated warnings are fully mitigated (first-party ASUS sourcing; the one dead Eneba snapshot's claims independently confirmed by ASUS). There is no factual error a corrections note could honestly document, so this is a clean APPROVE rather than APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS.
